invocation.sealed_entrypoint: The adapter entrypoint is copied into the content-addressed pack and the runner substitutes only that sealed path.
invocation.runtime_binding: The first argv token is an absolute regular executable whose bytes are hash-bound in the frozen config.
invocation.timeout_owner: the orchestrator terminates the adapter process tree at the frozen per-run wall-clock budget

observability_boundary: model_invocations records one adapter-level model invocation per attempt. A Codex CLI invocation may expose a codex_thread identifier; this is not represented as an HTTP or provider request identifier. The Codex CLI candidate launches no automatic second CLI invocation, records the child exit code and wall time, and never invents unobservable provider-client-internal retries.
token_boundary: input_tokens and output_tokens are provider-client observable totals. cached_input_tokens and cache_write_input_tokens are disjoint observable input subsets; reasoning_output_tokens is an observable output subset. An invocation with no terminal usage event is marked usage_observed=false and the run is infrastructure_failure rather than silently treated as a zero-cost completed run.
model_version_boundary: The hash-bound provider runtime is the local Codex CLI client. immutable_model_version is a frozen provider/operator attestation supplied to the client invocation; the JSONL stream does not independently attest the remote serving binary or provider-internal retries.
failure_boundary: For the Codex CLI candidate, infrastructure_failure_definition is the exact machine value codex_cli_nonzero_exit_or_missing_thread_or_missing_terminal_usage_or_runtime_error_or_forbidden_tool_or_ambiguous_build_accounting. Adapter-level semantic and infrastructure retry limits are zero; a failed run is retained as missing/terminal evidence under the missing-run policy that must be frozen separately before execution. Provider-client-internal retries are not observable in the JSONL stream and must be separately frozen or disclosed before execution.
tool_boundary: The Codex CLI candidate disables web search, apps, plugins, MCP discovery, multi-agent/collaboration, computer/browser/image tools, skills instructions, and related feature surfaces; it copies one plain auth.json into a fresh disposable CODEX_HOME for the invocation and gives spawned shell tools only the frozen allowlisted environment. Any observable forbidden-tool item makes the invocation an infrastructure failure. The final production agent image and its isolation probes remain separate prerequisites.
audit_rule: The orchestrator derives event counts from the complete trace, checks them against the response, frozen prices, and frozen budgets, hashes every adapter artifact plus the agent view, and never promotes an unobserved request, retry, token, or cost into evidence.
